chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), he said:
You will not find a bad man among forty bald men, and you will not find a good man among forty men with sparse beard hair; and a bad bald man is better than a good man with sparse beard hair.

key_terms.أصلع: Bald man (specifically lacking hair on the head)
key_terms.كوسج: Man with sparse or thin beard hair

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of baldness versus sparse beard hair in evaluating a person's character according to Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition from Imam Ali (a.s.) to illustrate that external physical traits, such as baldness or a sparse beard (kawsaj), are not reliable indicators of inner moral character. The narration suggests a cultural context where a sparse beard might have been associated with specific social or moral traits, yet the core lesson emphasizes looking beyond superficial appearances to discern true virtue. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between physical attributes and spiritual integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-166 According to the same documentation, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said, “
You will not find a bad man among even forty men who are bald in the front. You will not find any good man from amongst forty men who cannot grow any hair on the chin.”
